comment: The Clean-specific DECLARATION FORMS the pinned grammar has and no earlier clean fixture reached. The four pre-existing clean fixtures could not have caught any of them, because none of these node types occurs in their parse trees — which is what the F6 spec->fixture coverage gate exists to detect. Measured corpus sizes, every one of which published NOTHING before this round: macro_definition 583, special_member 507, class_context 474, generic_case_definition 52, derive_declaration 43, foreign_export 41, fixity_declaration 17, generic_declaration 11. Written the way this grammar accepts it, with the generic forms taken from clean-stdlib/StdGeneric.{dcl,icl} and the special/foreign/fixity forms from Clyde/Cocoa, so the fixture is real Clean rather than an invention. Every expectation key used here is one script/m14/run-fixtures.ts actually implements.

expectSymbols.name: Sized
expectSymbols.comment: class_declaration — AND THE MODULE-QUALIFIED IDENTITY (2026-10-29). A module-level symbol carries `Module.name` so the incoming gate can read a `.dcl`/`.icl` pair as ONE declaration (its `--binding-collapse` requires a non-empty qualifiedName that differs from the bare name; the store's file-scope fallback `qualifiedName = name` is not a qualification). MEASURED on the 312-file arm: references ambiguous 1,808 -> 1,011, exports 40 -> 12, 1,287 keys collapsed. A revert is caught HERE and by clean/module-level-qualified-name-dropped.

expectSymbols.name: sizeOf
expectSymbols.comment: the CLASS MEMBER carries NO module-level qualifiedName — the control for the row above. A member's identity is its OWNER's (`Sized.sizeOf`, which `pool-worker.ts:1228` derives from `scope` at the store boundary, and which is the spelling `overrides`/`implements` endpoints are written in), so the module-qualification pass runs one level ABOVE it. `null` pins the ABSENT form: a revert that qualified EVERY symbol, members included, would fail here.

expectSymbols.name: sizeOf
expectSymbols.comment: class_member -> type_signature, an ABSTRACT member: the class declares it and nothing here defines it

expectSymbols.name: MaxBound
expectSymbols.comment: macro_definition with a `constructor` name node — the kind is `macro` (the kind the store already has for Rust macro_rules!), and a macro IS in the export surface

macro_definition with a `parenthesized_name` name node — the second of the four name shapes the grammar allows. declarationName's comma/brace test is what stops the grammar's mis-shape for a PATTERN (`(<*>, <>)`) from publishing a name no source declares.

expectSymbols.name: bimap
expectSymbols.comment: generic_declaration — a class over TYPES rather than values, so an `interface` carrying generic parameters

expectSymbols.name: bimap
expectSymbols.comment: generic_case_definition — the THIRD shape that defines a callable. The two bimap{|…|} case equations merge into one function symbol with the case kinds recorded; the merge key carries the OWNER, so the generic's Interface and its case function stay two symbols instead of the definition overwriting the interface.

expectSymbols.name: Int::instance
expectSymbols.comment: instance Sized Int — the container is NAMESPACED under its target (`<target>::instance`, the Rust lane's `<target>::impl`), not named after it. TWO instances in this file target `Int` (L62 plain, L156 constrained by `{#}`) and they are two containers with this one name at two lines; `expectSymbolCount` below pins that neither overwrites the other.

expectSymbols.name: sizeOf
expectSymbols.comment: the INSTANCE's own member, a separate symbol from the class member because the merge key carries the owner

expectSymbols.name: strlen
expectSymbols.comment: foreign_export — a real callable and an explicit export

expectSymbols.name: helper
expectSymbols.comment: a `with` BLOCK binder, owned by the frame that encloses it

expectSymbols.name: delta
expectSymbols.comment: a `where` BLOCK binder declared by a local SIGNATURE; the signature's types join to the definition on the same frame+owner key, which is why delta carries returnType=!Int

expectSymbols.name: bump
expectSymbols.comment: the second binder in the same `where` block

expectSymbols.name: leadingExport
expectSymbols.comment: `foreign export` BEFORE its definition — the common `.icl` order. ONE symbol, anchored at the definition (L130), with the export SITE kept as `metadata.foreignExportLine` = L128 rather than lost when the range moved.

expectSymbols.name: trailingExport
expectSymbols.comment: `foreign export` AFTER its definition — legal in a `.dcl`, and the case the first implementation got wrong: the early `return` for an existing symbol dropped the export whole, so the function lost its FFI marker. Anchored at the definition (L133), `foreignExportLine` = L134.

expectSymbolCount.name: bimap
expectSymbolCount.comment: the generic (Interface) and its case function (Function) share a name because in Clean they are the same entity at two levels

expectSymbolCount.name: sizeOf
expectSymbolCount.comment: the class member and the instance member

expectSymbolCount.name: Int::instance
expectSymbolCount.comment: TWO instances target `Int` here — `instance Sized Int` (L62) and `instance Sized {#} Int` (L156) — and each publishes its own container. The merge key carries the line, so a mutant that keyed containers on the name alone would collapse them into one and fail here.

expectSymbolCount.name: leadingExport
expectSymbolCount.comment: the `foreign export`, the signature and the definition are ONE function symbol, so `equals: 1` — a second row here would mean the merge broke

expectSymbolCount.name: trailingExport
expectSymbolCount.comment: same for the late-export order: one symbol, not two

expectTypeParameters.comment: `generic bimap a b | bimap b a :: .a -> .b` — the two `parameter` field type variables, and `exact` so a mutant that duplicates or appends a name fails

expectReturnType.comment: the where-local's OWN signature `delta :: !Int` gives the local a result type
the CLASS member's signature `sizeOf :: a -> !Int` gives the abstract Method a result type

expectParameters.comment: `rewriteTag :: !Wrapper !String -> !Wrapper` — the domain's two `argument` types paired with the definition's two `pattern` fields POSITIONALLY. One pattern field is one parameter: a destructuring pattern would be one parameter of a tuple type, not several.

expectVisibility.comment: and the frame that owns them stays public — the local exclusion does not leak upward

expectExports.name: MaxBound
expectExports.comment: CHANGED KIND: a macro is exported. A Clean module-level macro is part of the module's interface like anything else, and the export list previously had no `macro` member at all because the analyzer published no macros.

forbidExports.name: helper
forbidExports.comment: a `with` binder is not part of the module's surface (M11.11 §2) — the exclusion is now stated in emitExports rather than being a side effect of the symbol not existing

forbidExports.name: delta
forbidExports.comment: a `where` binder is not part of the module's surface

forbidExports.name: inner
forbidExports.comment: a record FIELD is not a module-level name; its membership rides `contains`

forbidExports.name: Int
forbidExports.comment: CHANGED: `instance Sized Int` used to put `Int` in this module's export surface — a phantom export of a StdEnv type. The container is `Int::instance` of kind `impl` now, which is not exportable.

forbidExports.name: Int::instance
forbidExports.comment: an implementation is not part of a module's interface

forbidSymbols.name: a
forbidSymbols.comment: a class's or generic's type parameter is a binding, not a symbol

forbidSymbols.name: Ord
forbidSymbols.comment: an imported class named by a context is not a symbol of this file

forbidSymbols.name: a
forbidSymbols.comment: a POLYMORPHIC instance publishes no symbol either. `instance Sized {!} a` and `instance List [] a where` are real declarations, but naming their Class symbol after the type variable would put `a` in the symbol table — the same collision the row above forbids for a class's own type parameter. Their members are owned by the CLASS instead, so `contains` still resolves.

expectRelationships.comment: CHANGED: a class's SUPERCLASS CONTEXT is a reference to the class it constrains on. `class Sized a | Ord a` — spec gap CL-G3, 474 corpus sites, every one of which published nothing before. The line is the CONTEXT node's own line.

the instance edge, on the class NAME node's line (M59 #825: for an implements edge the class name is the name-bearing node)  TIER: `structural` — `instance Sized Int` names a class declared in THIS file, so the instance is a structural fact rather than a reference to an imported class

CHANGED: `derive bimap PAIR` is the same shape as an instance — an implementation of a class AT a type — so it is an `implements` edge from the derived type to the generic, on the generic name's line. All 43 corpus sites published nothing before.

CHANGED: a `special` block declares the TYPES the enclosing callable is specialised for, not a new NAME — the variable is the signature's own type parameter. One `references` edge per special type, on the TYPE's own line. 507 special_member corpus sites published nothing before.

the generic CASE function is contained by the module on its own line — line 52, the FIRST of the two `bimap{|…|}` case equations, because the clauses are alternative definitions of one symbol and the symbol is anchored where the function BEGINS (its range ends at line 53). Pinning 53 pinned last-write-wins on a keyed map, which put `isBid` on the wrong line in the M12 differential until it was fixed.

a `with` block's binder is reachable as a call target by its SCOPED identity — the resolution walks the scope stack, so a local is only ever a target from inside its own scope  TIER: `reference_qualified` — the target is a QUALIFIED identity (`<frame>.<name>`), so it is identified by reference rather than being a bare binding; the `usage_contextual` default is pinned by `reportTwice` in expression-shapes
CHANGED: `w.inner` is a record FIELD READ and the field is declared by this file, so the edge is provable rather than inferred
CHANGED: `{ w & tag = s }` is a record UPDATE; the field name is read from the `update_field` node rather than by zipping the parallel `field`/`value` field lists
a record FIELD's declared type is a reference from the field
a macro is in the export surface, and the edge says so on the macro's own line
an explicit `foreign export` is in the export surface

instance Sized {!} a — the constraint `{!}` names NO type, so the target is the type VARIABLE `a`. The first-argument rule named this instance `{!}`; the `namedChild(0)` rule named it whatever the brace node's first child was.

instance Sized {32#} Real — the constraint carries a LEVEL (32) as well as a type, and the first-argument rule named this instance `32`. An `array_type` holding both is the shape that forced the walk to be structural rather than positional.

instance Sized {#Char} — a SINGLE argument that is a type, not a constraint: `{#Char}` has a `dotted_type` child where `{#}` and `{!}` have none. This is the case a `text.startsWith('{')` test gets wrong.

instance Sized {#} Int — the plain constrained case, and the one the shared F5 oracle's differential caught: it derives `implements Int -> Array` from clean-stdlib's `_SystemArray.dcl` and the analyzer was emitting `implements {#} -> Array`.

`instance Sized {!} a` is POLYMORPHIC — its target is the type variable `a` — so it emits this `implements` edge but publishes NO Class symbol: a symbol named `a` would collide with the spec's rule that a type parameter is a BINDING, which `forbidSymbols` already pins. `meta.isPolymorphicInstance` is what says why this edge has no symbol at its source, and the tier stays `structural` because the class IS declared in this file — the tier answers how the class is known, and a variable target does not weaken that.

forbidRelationships.comment: a class's type parameter is not a symbol and not a member
a generic's own context (`generic bimap a b | bimap b a`) is SELF-REFERENTIAL and a symbol cannot reference itself; the context is recorded in the symbol's `genericContext` metadata instead
`special a=Int` is a TYPE REFERENCE, not a construction: no `Int` value is built
the two `bimap{|…|}` case equations are two CASES of one function, not a self-call
the FP pin: the RECEIVER of a field access is a value, not a field
a parameter name is not a record field
a generic's parameter is a BINDING, not a type reference
a class owns its members, not the generics declared beside it

THE MISNAMING, pinned as forbidden: a bare uniqueness constraint is not an instance's target type. Also forbidden are `32` (a constraint LEVEL), `{}` and `{!}` — all four were emitted by earlier versions of `instanceTargetName`.
a constraint LEVEL is not a type; `{32#}` has a `number` child and a `dotted_type` child, and only the latter names a type

expectRelationshipCount.comment: the `special` block's `Int` is ONE edge. `Int` also appears in `sizedOf`'s own signature, but that is a different SOURCE, and dedupe is keyed source|type|target|line

the generic and its case function share a name; the name-keyed export dedupe emits one edge, and which of the two symbols it names is decided by first-wins — pinned so the number cannot silently change

expectMetadata.comment: the full pattern set this fixture's constructs mark — the round's whole point is that these eleven marks existed for 583 + 507 + 474 + 52 + 43 + 41 + 17 + 11 corpus sites that carried no mark at all

expectSymbolMetadata.comment: the FFI claim is per-LINE like every other one the analyzer makes, so the export site is recorded even though the symbol's range is the definition's

a LATE `foreign export` flags the existing symbol instead of being dropped; `foreignExportLine` is the first export line seen, so a file that exports the same name twice does not move the recorded site
